requirements.requirement: On node1, persistently disable IPv4 ICMP redirect and source-routed packet acceptance.
requirements.summary: The final persistent sysctl configuration disables both controls for all, default, ens2, and lo. Before reboot, every observed IPv4 scope reported both values as 0. After an acknowledged reboot with a changed boot ID, the configuration remained present and every scope again reported both values as 0; networking, SSH, and systemd-sysctl recovered successfully.

overall_summary: The required IPv4 hardening is fully satisfied and was directly verified before and after reboot. The node-restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity, and recovered services and networking were all captured and independently corroborated by lifecycle observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. cmd-3fa348b6221c4809 installed the required all/default settings but direct verification showed existing interfaces still enabled; cmd-fe01a0eaf7184594 then refined the same task configuration to cover those interfaces. The reboot was required by the provider evidence protocol and also directly validated persistence. No failed services, package damage, unsafe exposure, or abandoned task artifacts were observed after execution.
